name: Lam Wai-ying
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2016-2025); Wikidata (2018)
forbes_bio: Lam and her husband Yeung Kin-man own Hong Kong's Biel Crystal, which makes screens for smartphones.
Lam, Biel's chairman, owns 49% of the business; Yeung holds 51%.
Biel is the largest supplier of glass screens for cell phones, tablets and watches to Apple and employs 90,000 people around the world.
While weakening iPhone demand may affect shipments to Apple, they also supply to Samsung and Sony and have stated they expect stable revenue.
Since 2021 Biel has filed twice for a Hong Kong IPO but it never materialized.

name: Daniel Mate
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2012-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Wikidata (2025)
forbes_bio: Daniel Mate is the former head of zinc at commodities giant Glencore.
Mate joined Marc Rich & Co. in 1988 in Switzerland, six years before the firm was bought out by management and changed its name to Glencore.
Mate rose to co-directing the zinc, copper and lead commodity department in 2000. He retired in July 2020.

name: Stephen Butt
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2023-2025); Hurun Global (2026); Sunday Times Rich List (2020)
forbes_bio: Stephen Butt is Texas grocery chain H-E-B's President of Shareholder Relations and its Central Market Division, a brand focused on specialty foods from around the world, and serves on the board.
His brother, Howard Butt III, is H-E-B's CEO and his uncle, Charles Butt, is chairman.
Based in San Antonio, H-E-B has 455 stores in Texas and Mexico and does $50 billion in annual revenue.
Butt's great-grandmother, Florence Butt, started the company in 1905.
forbes_facts: H-E-B gives 5% of pretax profits to charity.

name: Sylvan Adams
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2026)
forbes_bio: Sylvan Adams is the son of Marcel Adams (died August 2020, at age 100), who founded Canadian real estate company Iberville Developments.
Iberville owns and manages a nearly eight million square feet of real estate (shopping centers, office spaces, industrial properties, and residential assets), according to Adams.
He was named president and CEO of Iberville in 1994. Three years later he bought out family member stakes in the company and became sole holder of Iberville Developments.
Adams emigrated to Israel with his wife Margaret in 2015. The couple lives in Tel Aviv.
A philanthropist, Adams is a Giving Pledge signatory and estimates he has donated or invested over $100 million in various organizations, initiatives and projects.

name: Tor Peterson
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2012-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Tor Peterson is the only American among the five-person cadre of billionaires to earn their fortunes at Swiss commodities-trading powerhouse Glencore.
After six years of trading commodities at Phibro-Salomon in New York, he joined Glencore in 1992 and leads marketing operations for its coal division.
He owns a minority stake in Glencore, which trades on the London Stock Exchange.
In 2021, Peterson stepped down from his role at Glencore as the commodities firm shook up its leadership ranks.
forbes_facts: He attended boarding school in Switzerland, college at Duke in the U.S. and lives in Zug.
His brother, Gunnar, is a personal trainer in Los Angeles whose client list has reportedly included Sophia Vergara, Angelina Jolie and Kim Kardashian.

name: Pedro de Godoy Bueno
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2022); Forbes annual (2020-2022); Hurun Global (2021-2023)
forbes_bio: At age 29, Pedro de Godoy Bueno is Brazil's youngest billionaire. He is CEO of Brazilian laboratory firm Diagnosticos da America SA.
His late father, Edson de Godoy Bueno, was Brazil's richest healthcare billionaire. His sister, Camilla de Godoy Bueno Grossi, is also billionaire.
Edson died of a heart attack in 2017 at age 73 and left most of his fortune to his children, Pedro and Camilla.
His father's first wife, Dulce Pugliese de Godoy Bueno, cofounded healthcare firm Amil and is also a billionaire.
Pedro, who became CEO of DASA at 24, married his longtime partner Herrmann Hoffmann in 2018 at the Gavea Golf Club, a posh Rio de Janeiro club.

name: Stephen Rubin
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2015-2025); Hurun Global (2016-2026); Sunday Times Rich List (2020)
forbes_bio: Stephen Rubin is the chairman of Pentland Group, one of the U.K.'s largest sports apparel companies.
Rubin owns an estimated 49% of Pentland, which owns brands like Speedo and Berghaus and a majority stake in publicly-traded JD Sports Fashion.
His parents started Pentland in 1932 as a shoe wholesaler. In 1959, he joined the firm and a decade later, after his father died, took over as chair.
The company paid $77,500 for a 55% stake in Reebok USA in 1981, then offloaded the investment for $770 million in 1991.
forbes_facts: In 2002, Rubin was named an Officer of the British Empire for his services to business and to human rights. It is one of the highest honors in the country.

name: Manuel Lao Hernández
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2014-2025); Hurun Global (2016-2026); Wikidata (2025)
forbes_bio: Manuel Lao Hernandez founded Cirsa, a multinational casino company. He sold it to Blackstone for an estimated $2.6 billion (including debt) in 2018.
He started the business in 1978 and expanded it to nine countries in Latin America and Europe. He still owns Cirsa's Argentina operations.
His three children all worked for the family business, which was based just outside of Barcelona.
Today, through his Nortia investment firm, Lao Hernandez has interests in infrastructure, real estate and  leisure and entertainment.
forbes_facts: As a hobby, Lao Hernandez grows bonsai trees.
He has a foundation named after him that has organized a poker tournament in which people with disabilities compete to have a wish fulfilled.

name: Carmen Riu Guell
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026)
forbes_bio: Carmen Riu Guell's fortune is derived from Riu Hotel & Resorts, which she owns and runs with her brother Luis Riu, also a billionaire.
She manages the business through the family's holding company, Saranja, which has a portfolio of 98 hotels in 21 countries.
Under her leadership as co-CEO, the group saw over $4.5 billion in revenue and $150 million in net profit in 2024.
Born in Mallorca, she is a third-generation heir of the Riu hospitality group, which she took over after her father's passing in the 1990s.
While not known for large-scale philanthropy, at least not publicly, she has backed local Balearic community projects and tourism-related initiatives.
forbes_facts: Guell is credited with steering the company through both the 2008 financial crisis and the COVID-19 tourism collapse without selling a single hotel.
